metadata.title: Credo, Marvell settle intellectual property battle over data center cable tech

content.text:
Investing.com -- Shares of Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd (NASDAQ:CRDO) climbed around 2% and Marvell Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MRVL) rose 0.5% in after-hours trading Tuesday after the chipmakers settled a patent dispute over high-speed data connectivity technology. The agreement clears a legal overhang in the rapidly expanding market for artificial intelligence data infrastructure, where both firms compete to supply critical hardware components.
Under the terms of the settlement, the two companies resolved disputes surrounding their respective patent rights for Active Electrical Cable (AEC) technology. While financial and licensing terms remain confidential, the accord brings a close to contentious intellectual property proceedings that had threatened to complicate commercial deployments.
The resolution specifically addresses challenges Marvell initiated against Credo's patents before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office in August 2025. Those filings included inter partes review proceedings, such as a challenge targeting Credo's U.S. Patent No. 11,012,252, which covers active ethernet and electrical cable innovations.
For Credo, which specializes in high-speed copper and optical interconnect solutions designed to link chips and clusters within AI data centers, the settlement removes a direct threat to its core intellectual property portfolio. Investors responded positively to the reduced legal uncertainty, lifting both stocks as the companies put the regulatory battle behind them.
